chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muhammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Daghshī, from a man from the people of Shām, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abān al-Zayyāt, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who married his paternal cousin, while the mother of his grandfather's concubine had breastfed him. Is she prohibited to the boy or not? He said, 'No.'

This is a report with a continuous chain, yet it is considered *mursal* (with a missing link or weak connection in the specific context of authority), and its ruling is that it does not contradict the sound reports with strong chains. If it were safe from that, it would be interpreted as: if the concubine had breastfed him with milk other than that of the grandfather, or if she had breastfed him with a type of nursing that does not cause prohibition, and if it were complete nursing, then her son would become his uncle (if the grandfather was from the father's side); and if the grandfather was from the mother's side, there is no basis there that necessitates prohibition.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine (mother of a child by her master)
key_terms.مَقْطُوعُ الْإِسْنَادِ: Continuous chain (referring to the specific scholarly assessment in this context)
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: Mursal (a type of hadith with a missing link or specific weakness in chain authority)

ai.seo_question: Does a grandfather's concubine's son become a prohibited uncle through breastfeeding?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS) to clarify that a grandfather’s concubine’s breastfeeding does not establish a direct mahram relationship for the grandson, as the link is indirect. The text further notes that even if the breastfeeding were complete, the resulting kinship would be that of an uncle (if the grandfather was paternal) or no prohibition at all (if maternal), distinguishing this from the primary *radāʿ* prohibitions derived from the mother.
